To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

thermal transport in amophous semiconducting materials is more complicated than previously expected, and that the thermal conductivity of such materials can be tuned over a wide range by controlling the sample geometry, the material composition, and the sample temperature.

thermal conductivity of amorphous semiconductor materials can be predicted by a simple model based on the phonon density of states, and that thermal conductivity of these materials can be tuned by controlling the phonon density-of-states through the introduction of point defects.

phonon transport properties of amorphorous semiconductors are determined by the relative contribution of three types of vibrations (propagons, diffuson, locon), which are in turn determined by the material structure, temperature, and sample size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the physics behind thermal transport in amophous semiconducting materials.
the fundamental physics of heat transfer at the nanoscale, which is the basis of thermal management of modern electronic devices and systems.
the thermal properties of semiconductor materials and nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

thermal transport in amophous materials, especially semiconductors is a complicated process that depends not only on the material properties and the sample size and temperature, but also on the preparation conditions.
thermal transport in amorphic materials is a complex phenomenon that is still not fully understood.
the thermal conductivity of amorphous Si can be reduced to a value close to the amorphous limit of 1.0 Wm−1K−1 by controlling the sample size, temperature, and/or the amorphous structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermal transport properties of amorphously disordered materials are more complicated than those of crystalline materials, but the physics of thermal transport in both types of materials are similar.
the thermal conductivity of amorphous semiconductor materials can be significantly reduced compared to that in their crystalline counterparts.
thermal transport in amorphic semiconductor materials is much more complicated than in their crystalline counterparts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the thermal properties of an amorphous semiconductor can be tuned by controlling its microstructure and composition, which is a key feature for the development of next-generation thermoelectric and thermophotonic devices.
thermal conductivity of amorphous semiconductor materials can be significantly reduced by engineering the material structure at the nanometer length scale.
phonon transport is more complicated in amorphous than in crystalline materials.
